Silver 2026 GMC Yukon AT4 Makes a Gloss Black Statement on Brand-New Vossen HFX-5 Alloy Wheels
7 photos
Photo: vossen / Instagram
If you were wondering about General Motors and what it’s been up to recently, we heard that the company has finally relented to hybrid peer pressure, and after watching Japanese and Korean automakers gain massive ground with their electrified models, they are finally ready to crave a piece of the HEV pie.
GM spent years building a cult for EV models, and now America is waging war against zero-emission vehicles and their sales are, naturally, nosediving. So, a change of scenery was in order, and after carmakers like Toyota or Kia profited massively from the current hybrid boom, the biggest of the US automakers will join the fray with three hybrid sport utility vehicles, namely the HEV options for the Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia, and Buick Enclave , according to a report from Reuters.
But even if that’s very interesting, we’re actually here to discuss an even larger SUV – the GMC Yukon, as an example that was thoroughly customized to stand out in any crowd was recently shared on social media by the good folks over at Miami, Florida-based Vossen . They have gotten their hands on a batch of cool pictures featuring another GM - this time around a Yukon AT4- after not long ago we saw them showcase a GMC Sierra HD Denali on Gloss Black Vossen HFX-5 wheels.
The company promises that the new Vossen HFX-5 alloys will make a statement, and they continue with this silver-over-black GMC Yukon AT4 that has loads of Gloss Black details, including the new set of rims, which are shod in massive all-terrain tires. The Vossen HFX-5 are hybrid forged alloy wheels offered in both a six-lug or eight-lug configuration, with the former present on the mighty full-size body-on-frame SUV.
The prices kick off at $525 for each wheel, and the options are 17 through 24-inch diameters with 8.5- to 12-inch widths and a ton of colorful finishes. Of course, the owner chose Gloss Black for the wheels to mix and match with other trim elements of the SUV. Otherwise, if you’re interested in buying a brand-new GMC Yukon of the refreshed fifth-generation variety, you’ll need a 2027 model year before thinking that the sky is the limit when it comes to customization options from the aftermarket realm.
So, a 2027 GMC Yukon kicks off at an MSRP of no less than $70,200 sans destination, with available seating for up to eight people, and the AT4 is 4WD only starting from $80,695 with the 5.3-liter V8 engine and a ten-speed automatic transmission. Of course, you can always change the powertrain to the 6.2-liter V8 or the 3.0-liter Duramax turbo diesel – maybe for the next model year GM will introduce the new 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter V8s from the Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra on their Chevy Tahoe and GMC Yukon cousins, too.
